global_scale_note: Fundus/body teaching crop; original mucosal thickness approximately 1.95 mm and block width approximately 3 mm. Gland transverse dimensions magnified 5x; eight enlarged axial rows and four sectors are teaching samples. External muscle layers are a partial crop. Molecular events and signal arrows are schematic.

sequences.mechanism: Gastric secretion leaves apical epithelial surfaces into a blind gland's lumen and reaches the organ lumen through its pit.

steps.caption: One surface pit receives several gland outlets. These openings share the gastric lumen; the pit itself is lined by surface mucous cells.
steps.overlay: Optional upward direction arrow in the existing pit opening; never through epithelium.

steps.caption: Follow one narrow lumen from the basal gland through its body and neck into the pit. The model shows three branches per representative pit.
steps.overlay: Optional directional line follows one source branch; no measured fluid speed or pressure.

steps.caption: The rounded gland base is blind and stays above muscularis mucosae. Its secretions travel upward; the basal end is not a duct through the wall.
steps.overlay: No downward flow arrow.

schematic_limitations: Lumens are deliberately readable at enlarged transverse scale.
Intercellular display seams are not leakage routes.
Lumen continuity and basal closure require saved-mesh verification.
acceptance_conditions: No route exits through chief dome or crosses muscularis mucosae.
Source branch connects visually to its own pit outlet.

sequences.mechanism: Apical surface protection maintains a qualitative pH gradient while gastric contents remain acidic.

steps.caption: Surface mucous cells cover the exposed surface and pits. Their apical secretion forms an adherent protective gel.
steps.overlay: Optional translucent gel band above the existing surface, labeled schematic and not an added anatomical part.

steps.caption: Bicarbonate enters the gel from the surface epithelium and neutralizes acid diffusing toward the cells. Near-surface pH can remain close to neutral.
steps.overlay: Qualitative gradient: acidic organ lumen to protected surface. Use descriptive endpoints, not numerical pH measurements.

steps.caption: The stable mucus layer also restricts pepsin access to the epithelium. Protection depends on secretion, epithelial integrity, and tissue support working together.
steps.overlay: Optional pepsin symbol stays in the organ-lumen context; no simulated erosion.

schematic_limitations: No mucus gel, bicarbonate transporter or tight junction is independently meshed.
No physiological gel thickness, pH field or acid diffusion rate is computed.
Gland outlet transport through mucus is not modeled as a literal permanent tunnel.
acceptance_conditions: Caption distinguishes surface gel from gland-lumen secretion.
Overlay does not occlude all pit openings or imply impermeable acid-proof plastic.

sequences.mechanism: Parietal cells provide apical acid output and intrinsic factor with distinct downstream roles.

steps.caption: The large bulging parietal cells remain epithelial cells. Their acid-secreting canaliculi communicate with the gland lumen.
steps.overlay: Canaliculus is caption/inset context; it is not resolved by this mesh.

steps.caption: Apical H+/K+-ATPase exchanges H+ for K+. Luminal chloride accompanies acid secretion; stimulated membrane recycling increases secretory surface.
steps.overlay: Optional H+ and Cl− arrow to existing gland lumen, then pit; no acid arrow into lamina propria.

steps.caption: Human parietal cells also make intrinsic factor. Its role in vitamin B12 absorption is completed in the terminal ileum, beyond this crop.
steps.overlay: Intrinsic factor uses a separate caption/legend from H+; no stomach B12-uptake arrow.

schematic_limitations: No intracellular canaliculus, tubulovesicle, pump molecule or drug-response simulation is present.
Intrinsic factor is not the acid-neutralizing surface gel.
acceptance_conditions: No vitamin uptake is depicted through the gastric epithelium.

sequences.mechanism: Basal chief cells produce an enzyme precursor that enters the apical gland route.

steps.caption: Chief cells predominate in the deeper gland. Basal rough endoplasmic reticulum supports protein production; secretory granules face the lumen.
steps.overlay: Rough ER and granules are explanatory inset context, not literal purple cell geometry.

steps.caption: Pepsinogen is released toward the gland lumen and then the pit. The precursor becomes active pepsin in the acidic luminal environment.
steps.overlay: Optional precursor symbol moving upward through an existing branch; no movement through the blind dome.

steps.caption: Different epithelial populations contribute complementary luminal products. Surface protection permits digestion alongside a living gastric wall.
steps.overlay: Use distinct precursor and acid labels; no active-enzyme cloud inside lamina propria.

schematic_limitations: No secretion rate, granule depletion or protein-digestion model is computed.
Chief dome is a basal boundary, not a literal giant chief cell.
acceptance_conditions: The basal region stays blind during the entire sequence.

sequences.mechanism: A blood-borne endocrine input recruits local basolateral paracrine control of parietal acid output.

steps.caption: The represented endocrine population is ECL. Human ECL cells lie along the basal gland epithelium; their processes approach neighboring parietal cells.
steps.overlay: No direct lumen-contact claim. Requires the basal ECL construction correction before anatomical acceptance.

steps.caption: Gastrin comes from antral G cells outside this crop and reaches ECL receptors through the circulation.
steps.overlay: Incoming annotation labeled 'circulating gastrin from antrum'; unmeshed capillary delivery must remain schematic.

steps.caption: ECL histamine acts locally on parietal H2 receptors. This is a basal/interstitial paracrine route, separate from gastric juice.
steps.overlay: Short schematic histamine arrow outside gland lumen; receptor detail is explanatory context.

steps.caption: A basal regulatory input can increase apical acid secretion. Keep the two routes visibly distinct.
steps.overlay: Separate labeled basal signal and apical output arrows; no histamine delivery into the pit.

schematic_limitations: Baseline ee sectors reach the lumen and therefore require correction or explicit schematic qualification.
ECL is not a stand-in for G, D, ghrelin and serotonin populations.
No antrum, microcirculatory branch, receptor kinetics or endocrine feedback timing is modeled.
acceptance_conditions: Corrected ECL cells lack luminal contact.
Gastrin remains an off-crop incoming signal.
Histamine arrows remain interstitial and never run inside gland lumen or lymphatic vessels.

sequences.mechanism: A neck region supplies mucus to the gland while an adjacent progenitor region sustains epithelial renewal.

steps.caption: The neck lies beneath the pit and contains mucous neck cells interspersed with other gland cells.
steps.overlay: No extra stem-cell mesh is implied by the combined part name.

steps.caption: Neck-cell mucus enters the gland lumen. This local secretion should be distinguished from the protective surface-cell gel.
steps.overlay: Short luminal arrow; do not draw neck cells as goblet cells.

steps.caption: Progenitors near the pit–gland junction replenish epithelial populations. Renewal is a slower process than secretion.
steps.overlay: Optional qualitative migration annotation; no lineage timing or cell-motion animation on the eight-row sample.

schematic_limitations: Combined isthmus/neck identity does not isolate stem cells.
Literal cell lifetimes and differentiation histories are not inferred from schematic rows.
acceptance_conditions: Surface and neck mucus remain different teaching concepts.
Stem cells are presented as contextual content unless separately modeled.

sequences.mechanism: The submucosal support compartment supplies the mucosa and provides neural access while remaining separate from gland drainage.

steps.caption: Blood vessels and lymphatic vessels course within supporting tissue beneath the mucosa. Their lumens are distinct from gastric pits and glands.
steps.overlay: Label each vessel type; keep artery, vein and lymph routes independent.

steps.caption: Fine mucosal capillaries supply gland and surface cells within the thin lamina propria. The current larger submucosal vessel meshes do not show that complete microcirculation.
steps.overlay: Capillary supply is caption context, not a claimed physical connection between the displayed parallel vessels.

steps.caption: The displayed submucosal neural network represents local support. Gastric secretion also receives vagal and myenteric neural inputs outside this simplified network.
steps.overlay: Highlight the network without assigning unverified neuron identities, synapses or measured conduction.

schematic_limitations: No complete arterial-capillary-venous connection or lymphatic drainage territory is represented.
The neural network is schematic; intestinal submucosal circuit density must not be assumed for gastric tissue.
No vagal trunk, immune traffic, bicarbonate recycling or perfusion simulation is provided.
acceptance_conditions: Vessel lumen openings stay readable in native cutaways.
No gastric juice enters vascular or lymphatic lumens.
Caption exposes microcirculation and circuit limits.

sequences.mechanism: Separate smooth-muscle orientations support gastric mechanical functions, under neural regulation and electrical coordination that extend beyond the crop.

steps.caption: Compare oblique, circular and longitudinal fascicle directions. The block samples the wall; it does not close around an entire stomach lumen.
steps.overlay: Direction glyphs may follow existing bundles; retain separately selectable layers.

steps.caption: Myenteric ganglia occupy the intermuscular region. Motor regulation is distinct from electrical slow-wave generation by interstitial cells of Cajal, which are not separately modeled.
steps.overlay: Neural highlight only; do not label the yellow network as ICC or a pacemaker organ.

steps.caption: Rugal support permits changes in fold shape as the stomach fills. Whole-stomach accommodation, mixing and emptying require anatomy beyond this fixed local crop.
steps.overlay: Static comparison and caption only; no global peristaltic deformation or ruga flattening animation asserted.

schematic_limitations: No ICC population, whole circumference, greater-curvature pacemaker, antrum, pyloric sphincter or chyme domain is modeled.
A roughly three-cycles-per-minute human organ rhythm is not a universal contraction rate for each displayed fascicle.
Do not infer wave speed, emptying rate, retropulsion or fundus-specific rhythm from this mixed fundus/body crop.
acceptance_conditions: Three layer identities and real intermuscular location remain readable.
No local 3/min contractile animation is presented as measured physiology.
The partial-wall and schematic scale note remains accessible before motion context.
